We found 15 things from 12 sources and 2 places where sources disagree, and turned them into 16 questions for the developer's teams. Here is what stood out first.

Three questions to start with

Put these to the developer in writing. Each says who should answer and what a good answer looks like.

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    Which company is the seller on my sale and purchase agreement for Creek Bay Tower B (Emaar Properties, another Emaar company, or a joint venture with Dubai Holding), and is it the developer registered for DLD project 4198?

    Why it matters. Your rights run against the company on the agreement; sources differ on who is master developer of Dubai Creek Harbour.

    A good answer
    The SPA naming the seller, matching the DLD project record.
    Does not close it
    "It is an Emaar project."

    Where it appears: realestateclubdubai.com / area-guide/dubai-creek-harbour-master-plan-2026-distric…, a.land / blog/dubai-creek-harbour-emaar-s-new-city-development-p…, tohidfetrat.com / creek-bay-dubai-creek-harbour-construction-update-june-…

  2. Q2 Ask the accounts team, before booking

    Please give me the escrow account name, bank and number for DLD project 4198, so I can confirm it in the Dubai REST app before paying, and confirm every payment, including the booking amount, goes there.

    Why it matters. Off-plan payments in Dubai must go to the project's escrow account; paying anywhere else removes that protection.

    A good answer
    Account details that match the DLD record.
    Does not close it
    A request to pay a different account or a broker.

    Where it appears: tohidfetrat.com / creek-bay-dubai-creek-harbour-construction-update-june-…, joinoliva.com / blog/dubai-creek-harbour-off-plan-investment-guide

  3. Q3 Ask the sales team, before booking

    Agents describe the payment plan as 80/20 (10% down and seven instalments) and as 10/70/20. Which plan applies to my unit, and is each instalment tied to a date or to certified construction progress?

    Why it matters. Time-based instalments can run ahead of a site that, in June 2026, had 0.62% certified progress.

    A good answer
    The payment schedule annexed to the SPA, with each trigger stated.
    Does not close it
    An agent's summary.

    Where it appears: providentestate.com / new-projects/creek-bay-emaar-properties-dubai-creek-har…, laforet.ae / creek-bay-dubai-creek-harbour-guide, tohidfetrat.com / creek-bay-dubai-creek-harbour-construction-update-june-…, valley-dubai-sales.com / emaar-creek-bay-at-dubai-creek-harbour

Start here: the questions that matter most

Eight to put first. The full wording, the closing test and a place to track each are in "Every question, by stage".

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    Which company is the seller on my sale and purchase agreement for Creek Bay Tower B (Emaar Properties, another Emaar company, or a joint venture with Dubai Holding), and is it the developer registered for DLD project 4198?

    Your rights run against the company on the agreement; sources differ on who is master developer of Dubai Creek Harbour.

  2. Q2 Ask the accounts team, before booking

    Please give me the escrow account name, bank and number for DLD project 4198, so I can confirm it in the Dubai REST app before paying, and confirm every payment, including the booking amount, goes there.

    Off-plan payments in Dubai must go to the project's escrow account; paying anywhere else removes that protection.

  3. Q3 Ask the sales team, before booking

    Agents describe the payment plan as 80/20 (10% down and seven instalments) and as 10/70/20. Which plan applies to my unit, and is each instalment tied to a date or to certified construction progress?

    Time-based instalments can run ahead of a site that, in June 2026, had 0.62% certified progress.

  4. Q4 Ask the legal team, before signing

    The DLD-registered completion date is 30 April 2030. What handover date and grace period does my SPA state, and what compensation, if any, do I receive for each month of delay beyond it?

    Dubai agreements often allow a grace period; your remedy for delay depends on the SPA wording.

  5. Q5 Ask the legal team, before signing

    If I miss an instalment, what happens? Under Dubai Law 19 of 2017, below 60% completion the developer may cancel and keep up to 25% of the price. How much would I lose at each stage of my payment plan, and is there a grace period before default?

    With 10% paid and the project at an early stage, a missed payment could cost up to a quarter of the price.

  6. Q6 Ask the legal team, before signing

    Can I sell or assign my unit before completion? What percentage must be paid first, what is the developer's no-objection fee, and what DLD fees apply?

    Many buyers plan to resell before handover; developer rules on assignment decide whether that is possible.

  7. Q7 Ask the accounts team, before signing

    What is the total cost beyond the price: the DLD Oqood registration fee, administration fees, and the estimated service charge per square foot for Creek Bay?

    Fees and service charges change the real cost and the net rental yield.

  8. Q8 Ask the legal team, before signing

    How is my unit's area measured in the SPA (total or net), and what happens if the built area differs from the contract area, for example by more than 5%?

    Area variation clauses decide whether the price changes or you can withdraw.

All 16 questions follow the findings.

Stage of construction, possible link

At 0.62% certified progress in June 2026 and a registered completion of 30 April 2030, almost the whole build is still ahead. A time-based payment plan would run ahead of construction, and the default rules allow the developer to keep up to 25% if a buyer stops paying at this stage.
